text: Paul, an apostle—sent not from human beings, nor by any human being, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
Grace and peace to you from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you by the grace of Christ, and turning to a different gospel—
which is no gospel at all—except that there are some who are throwing you into confusion and want to distort the gospel of Christ.

versions.text: which is no gospel at all. There are some who are unsettling you and want to twist the gospel of Christ.
versions.explanation: The Greek εἰ μή links the two clauses ('except that...'), rather than starting a wholly new sentence; the connection clarifies that the 'different gospel' exists only because agitators are at work. 'Throwing into confusion' also captures ταράσσοντες more vividly than 'unsettling' for oral reading.

text: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let him be accursed.
As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone preaches to you a gospel other than the one you received, let him be accursed.
For am I now seeking the approval of people, or of God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.

versions.text: Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
versions.explanation: The connective γάρ ties this verse to the preceding curse formula and is currently untranslated. Rendering ἀνθρώπους consistently as 'people' within the verse also removes the awkward shift from 'human beings' to 'people' in successive clauses.

text: For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached is not of human origin.

versions.text: I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached is not of human origin.
versions.explanation: The connective γάρ, which introduces Paul's explanation of the preceding statement, is missing; adding 'For' preserves the logical flow of the argument.

text: I did not receive it from any human being, nor was I taught it; it came by a revelation of Jesus Christ.

versions.text: I did not receive it from any human being, nor was I taught it; I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
versions.explanation: The Greek has no repeated verb 'I received'; the phrase is simply 'through a revelation of Jesus Christ.' Keeping the genitive ambiguous ('of Jesus Christ') preserves both senses—revelation given by Christ and revelation whose content is Christ—rather than resolving it to 'from.'

text: You have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how relentlessly I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my people, and was far more zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
But when God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by his grace, was pleased
to reveal his Son in me so that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. Instead I went away into Arabia, and later returned to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
I saw none of the other apostles—only James, the Lord's brother.
In what I am writing to you, I assure you before God that I am not lying.
Then I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
I was personally unknown to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
They only kept hearing, "The man who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy."
And they glorified God because of me.
